blocks.text: COLOR VISION - FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS (FAQS)
blocks.html: COLOR VISION - FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS (FAQS)

blocks.text: - 1. Why is the FAA Changing their policy now?
blocks.html: • 1. Why is the FAA Changing their policy now?

blocks.text: Several factors necessitate the change: Proliferation of color displays, concern that current testing might not be adequate for the existing and future color-rich environment, poor standardization in administration of current tests, incorrect testing by some AMEs, and NTSB safety recommendation (for commercial pilots). Advances in testing technology and completion of test evaluations at the Civil Aerospace Medical Institute enabled the change.
blocks.html: Several factors necessitate the change: Proliferation of color displays, concern that current testing might not be adequate for the existing and future color-rich environment, poor standardization in administration of current tests, incorrect testing by some AMEs, and NTSB safety recommendation (for commercial pilots). Advances in testing technology and completion of test evaluations at the Civil Aerospace Medical Institute enabled the change.

blocks.text: - 2. If I am unable to obtain one of the computer-based tests, can the pilot be tested at a different location?

blocks.text: If the AME does not have an acceptable color vision test, they can issue a 3rd class medical certification with limitation #104. Do not defer.

blocks.text: - 3. Does the test need to be performed within 90 days of the AME exam?
blocks.html: • 3. Does the test need to be performed within 90 days of the AME exam?

blocks.text: NO. The FAA can accept a previous test result provided it is one of the acceptable computer-based tests. (E.g., Some individuals may have had this testing in the military. Those scores may be submitted.)
blocks.html: NO. The FAA can accept a previous test result provided it is one of the acceptable computer-based tests. (E.g., Some individuals may have had this testing in the military. Those scores may be submitted.)

blocks.text: - 4. Should the AME defer a new applicant if they are unable to pass any of the acceptable color vision screening tests?
blocks.html: • 4. Should the AME defer a new applicant if they are unable to pass any of the acceptable color vision screening tests?

blocks.text: NO. The AME should ISSUE a 3rd class medical certificate (if otherwise qualified) with limitation #104 “Valid for day visual flight rules [VFR] only.”
blocks.html: NO. The AME should ISSUE a 3rd class medical certificate (if otherwise qualified) with limitation #104 “Valid for day visual flight rules [VFR] only.”

blocks.text: - 5. Is the individual limited to taking only ONE of the computer-based tests?
blocks.html: • 5. Is the individual limited to taking only ONE of the computer-based tests?

blocks.text: NO. The individual can take any of the three acceptable computer-based tests. Passing ANY of the three is acceptable and failure of one test does not preclude an attempt to pass another.
blocks.html: NO. The individual can take any of the three acceptable computer-based tests. Passing ANY of the three is acceptable and failure of one test does not preclude an attempt to pass another.

blocks.text: - 6. Can the individual submit a test taken at home or a free trial version?
blocks.html: • 6. Can the individual submit a test taken at home or a free trial version?

blocks.text: NO. If a computer color vision test was done outside the AME’s office, the AME must verify that the results belong to the individual. To maintain test integrity, the test must be performed by a practitioner who can verify the individual’s identity (similar to an EKG). If the results of the test cannot be linked to a specific individual, it cannot be used.

If the results of the test cannot be linked to a specific individual, it cannot be used.

blocks.text: - 7. Will the individual be given a more restrictive certificate with this new policy?
blocks.html: • 7. Will the individual be given a more restrictive certificate with this new policy?

blocks.text: NO. Whatever the individual has walking into the AME’s office (e.g., LOE, restricted certificate/any class, unrestricted, failed) is what they will walk out with, unless they take a new color test.

blocks.text: - 8. Does the FAA require normal color vision for pilots?
blocks.html: • 8. Does the FAA require normal color vision for pilots?

blocks.text: Pilots must possess the ability to perceive colors necessary to discern cockpit display colors, aircraft signaling, and airport lighting for the safe performance of airman duties.
blocks.html: Pilots must possess the ability to perceive colors necessary to discern cockpit display colors, aircraft signaling, and airport lighting for the safe performance of airman duties.

blocks.text: - 9. What are common causes of acquired color vision deficiency?
blocks.html: • 9. What are common causes of acquired color vision deficiency?

blocks.text: This list is not all inclusive, but common causes include:
blocks.html: This list is not all inclusive, but common causes include:

blocks.text:
- Eye conditions such as glaucoma, age-related macular degeneration, retinal detachment, or cataracts.
- Brain and nervous system conditions such as Alzheimer’s, multiple sclerosis, or certain tumors.
- Medical conditions such as diabetes, alcoholism, leukemia.
- Medications such as Plaquenil (chloroquine or hydroxychloroquine), blood pressure medications, erectile dysfunction medications.
blocks.html:
• Eye conditions such as glaucoma, age-related macular degeneration, retinal detachment, or cataracts.

  • Medical conditions such as diabetes, alcoholism, leukemia.
  • Medications such as Plaquenil (chloroquine or hydroxychloroquine), blood pressure medications, erectile dysfunction medications.

blocks.text: 10. If the pilot has a special issuance for an eye or neurology condition, why do they now need an additional color vision test?
blocks.html: 10. If the pilot has a special issuance for an eye or neurology condition, why do they now need an additional color vision test?

blocks.text: Certain medical conditions or medications may cause a red/green or blue/yellow color deficiency. While we do not need to test everyone for an acquired color vision defect, conditions which may also have a color vision deficiency will require specific testing. The pilot should refer to their Letter of Authorization.

blocks.html: 11. How does an individual apply for a Color Vision Limitation removal or upgrade?

blocks.text: The individual can take any or all the acceptable computer-based tests. If they pass, they do not need further testing.

blocks.text: 12. Do I test all pilots with a new computer-based test as of January 1, 2025?
blocks.html: 12. Do I test all pilots with a new computer-based test as of January 1, 2025?

blocks.text: NO. See the Color Vision Flow Chart. The AME only needs to test NEW pilots, those with a limitation 16 or 17 who want it removed, or those with a current LOE or SODA who want to upgrade. The individual can take any or all the acceptable computer-based tests.

blocks.text: - 13. Will the FAA consider adding additional computer-based tests in the future?
blocks.html: • 13. Will the FAA consider adding additional computer-based tests in the future?

blocks.text: The FAA will consider approval for new computerized tests if the manufacturer provides reliability, validity, and sensitivity/specificity documentation along with evidence of cut scores aligning with those specified for CCT, CAD, and CCVT.
blocks.html: The FAA will consider approval for new computerized tests if the manufacturer provides reliability, validity, and sensitivity/specificity documentation along with evidence of cut scores aligning with those specified for CCT, CAD, and CCVT.

blocks.text: - 14. How many times can an individual take the same computer-based test?
blocks.html: • 14. How many times can an individual take the same computer-based test?

blocks.text: There is no limit to the number of trials allowed. However, if multiple attempts are unsuccessful, the AME should question if the problem is test taking skills or color vision deficiency.
blocks.html: There is no limit to the number of trials allowed. However, if multiple attempts are unsuccessful, the AME should question if the problem is test taking skills or color vision deficiency.

blocks.text: - 15. Does the AME have to upload the actual color vision test report, or can they notate Pass/Fail and add comments?
blocks.html: • 15. Does the AME have to upload the actual color vision test report, or can they notate Pass/Fail and add comments?

blocks.text: The AME must upload a copy of the score report into AMCS under tag “Eye-Color Vision Test Results.” AMCS can accept a photo of the results by uploading file types as PDF, DOC, DOCX, JPG, JPEG, and XPS.
blocks.html: The AME must upload a copy of the score report into AMCS under tag “Eye-Color Vision Test Results.” AMCS can accept a photo of the results by uploading file types as PDF, DOC, DOCX, JPG, JPEG, and XPS.

blocks.text: - 16. Can the AME accept a color vision test report brought in by the individual?
blocks.html: • 16. Can the AME accept a color vision test report brought in by the individual?

blocks.text: Like an EKG performed outside the AME office, the AME should verify the person tested and the testing facility. We can accept a test signed by a provider (preferably with their clinic information on the test results) or with an attached Detailed Clinical Progress Note (if performed in another clinic) with the correct pilot identification.

blocks.text: There is no change to the current requirements for ATCS at this time.

blocks.text: 18. If the individual is an ATCS who is also a pilot and is seeking pilot certification for the first time (considered a first-time pilot), must they be tested using one of the new CV testing options?
blocks.html: 18. If the individual is an ATCS who is also a pilot and is seeking pilot certification for the first time (considered a first-time pilot), must they be tested using one of the new CV testing options?

However, if the ATCS is a first-time pilot seeking pilot medical certification, they must take one of the computer-based tests.

rows: The AME must document the color vision test instrument used, version, answer sheet with the actual subject responses and the score. If MEDExpress is used the AME should fax or mail the results to the Flight Surgeon or may document the findings in Block 60.

AME office inspections: The inspector must visually inspect the condition of the color vision test instrument, for fading, fingerprints, pen, or pencil smudges; and lights used. Only a Macbeth Easel or a Verilux True Daylight Illuminator (F15T8VLX) are acceptable. Room lights must be off.

Any test device with a restricted test set, like the Titmus testers, generally have a high false alarm test. If a disproportionally high number of subjects are failing, it may be necessary to review the acceptability of that test instrument. Regional Medical Offices are expected to monitor this situation.
blocks.html:
SPECIAL INSTRUCTIONS

Test Administration

The AME must document the color vision test instrument used, version, answer sheet with the actual subject responses and the score. If MEDExpress is used the AME should fax or mail the results to the Flight Surgeon or may document the findings in Block 60.

AME Office Inspection

AME office inspections: The inspector must visually inspect the condition of the color vision test instrument, for fading, fingerprints, pen, or pencil smudges; and lights used. Only a Macbeth Easel or a Verilux True Daylight Illuminator (F15T8VLX) are acceptable. Room lights must be off.

False Negatives

Any test device with a restricted test set, like the Titmus testers, generally have a high false alarm test. If a disproportionally high number of subjects are failing, it may be necessary to review the acceptability of that test instrument. Regional Medical Offices are expected to monitor this situation.
